newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European bourses extend gains, Paris unsteady.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European bourses extend gains, Paris unsteady.

text.p: European bourses climbed steeply on Tuesday after many hit trading records the previous day but Paris made an unsteady start because of the strong showing by leftwing parties in parliamentary elections.

On the foreign exchange front, the dollar strengthened nearly a pfennig in early trade with the mark slipping against other European currencies as the French poll increased expectations of a softer European single currency.

Most attention was fixed on equities after ten European bourses, including Frankfurt and Zurich, scored trading peaks on Monday, encouraged by a big rally in Wall Street at its last session on Friday.

German stocks extended their bull run to surge to fresh records although some of the gains were eroded by mid-morning. "We need calm after the past two days," a dealer said, "this is a healthy sign in a market."
The star performers were steel group Thyssen AG and retailer Metro AG, both of which climbed strongly after releasing better-than-expected profit figures.
London, which was closed because of a public holiday on Monday, climbed 0.7 percent in early trade, its first opportunity to react to Wall Street's record close on Friday.
The bourse, Europe's biggest, shrugged off a weaker bond market, to put on 30.6 points to reach 4692.4 at one stage as cash-rich institutional investors looked to buy into the market.
"The Bund (German government bonds) has been hammered this morning after the French election result but the overall tone is still fairly bullish," one senior dealer said.

French election jitters unsettled bond markets across Europe because of worries over the future of the European Monetary Union following the outcome of the surprise victory for the Socialist coalition in the first round.
"If the Socialists get back into power, the chances of EMU going ahead on time certainly will be diminished," a trader said.

Some strategists believe the FTSE will itself scale new peaks soon, spurred on by a wall of cash that is set to flood the market with the June 2 flotation of the Halifax Building Society, the nation's biggest mortgage lender.
"As long as the Dow keeps rising there is little doubt that the FTSE will break through 4,700," the trader said.

Paris stocks were still under the cloud of the first round election results. After plunging four percent on Monday, its biggest one-day loss in four years, the bourse slipped in and out of profit in early trade.
French shares opened 0.72 percent lower at 2641.88 points on the CAC-40 index but managed to struggle into the plus column by mid-morning.
Dealers said the announcement by Alain Juppe that he would not return as prime minister even if the centre-right was re-elected would not help shares.

"Our feeling is that Juppe either resigned too late or too early. It's a joker but it has not been well played," said Olivier Blitz of IFF, adding he saw the CAC-40 sliding to 2,600 before the end of the week.
In currency markets, the dollar was boosted by the fresh uncertainty over EMU following the French vote.

"The French election results after the first round do not derail EMU (European Monetary Union) but they suggest that when EMU does occur it will be a soft currency," said Nick Stamenkovic, economist at DKB International.
The dollar had strengthened to 1.6970 marks compared to 1.6899 in late trade on Monday. Against the yen, it was little changed at 116.18 yen.
Analysts said recent comments from Japanese officials have helped steady the dollar againmst the yen after it sank to five-month lows below 112.00 yen last week.
Elsewhere, the Czech crown was hit hard after the central bank (CNB) eliminated the band within which it had moved against a mark/dollar basket.
The crown was fixed at 19.5 to the mark, compared to the previous fix of 18.08, and 33.1 to the dollar, as against 30.5.
STOCK PRICES AT 0930 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was was up 27.3 points to 4,689.1.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 4.78 points at 2,659.66.
Frankfurt's DAX index was up 12.9 points at 3,670.67.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6970 marks and 116.18 yen compared with 1.6899 marks and 116.33 yen in late European trade on Monday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $343.55 ounce, compared to $343.10 in late trade on Monday. Silver was unchanged at $4.75.
